title: Set responses and situational phrases — どうぞ
summary: どうぞ is a polite word to offer, invite or give permission: “please / go ahead”. It is used in set phrases such as どうぞお入りください and お先にどうぞ. It does not change form and can also stand alone.

patterns.form: どうぞ＋（お）動詞ください
patterns.gloss: Please ～ (どうぞお入りください)

patterns.form: お先に／こちらへ＋どうぞ

body.p: Use どうぞ when you hand something over, invite someone in, or let someone go first: どうぞ、お入りください. Often a gesture goes with it.
As a reply to ～てもいいですか (May I ～?), どうぞ means “Yes, go ahead.” By itself it is a natural, polite answer.
～てください is a request for the listener to do something. どうぞ gives the listener the choice to take or do. Using both softens the tone: どうぞ、座ってください.

examples.ja: 「どうぞ、お入（はい）りください。」

pitfalls: どうぞ is for offering or permitting. To ask for a favor, use どうか or ～てください / お願いします.
Do not use どうぞ to refuse. Say けっこうです or すみません instead.
